description: The security domain concerned with controlling who or what may access systems, information, and system resources, and what authorized users are permitted to do.

A sophisticated and well-resourced adversary that uses multiple attack techniques, operates over an extended period, adapts to defensive measures, and seeks sustained access to achieve objectives such as information exfiltration or mission disruption.
The security domain concerned with ensuring personnel understand cybersecurity risks and receive the training needed to perform their security-related responsibilities.
An authorized third-party organization that conducts CMMC certification assessments.
The security domain concerned with assessing security requirements and controls, identifying deficiencies, and monitoring the effectiveness of security protections.

term: CMMC Assessors and Instructors Certification Organization
description: The organization responsible for training, testing, authorizing, certifying, and recertifying CMMC certified assessors, instructors, and professionals.
A code used to identify commercial or government entities that conduct business with the federal government.
An individual certified within the CMMC ecosystem to perform CMMC assessment activities and, when appropriately qualified, participate in Level 2 certification assessments.
An individual certified by the CAICO to perform CMMC instructional duties for eligible CMMC certification candidates.

An individual certified within the CMMC ecosystem who has demonstrated foundational knowledge of the CMMC model and may participate in authorized assessment activities within the limits of the credential.
The codification of the general and permanent rules published in the Federal Register by departments and agencies of the United States Government.
A senior organizational official responsible for information technology strategy, governance, resources, and oversight of information systems and related technology capabilities.
The security domain concerned with establishing and maintaining secure system configurations and controlling changes to systems, components, and software.

The Department of Defense program for assessing contractor and subcontractor implementation of cybersecurity requirements applicable to Federal Contract Information and Controlled Unclassified Information.
The Department of Defense program office responsible for administration and oversight of the CMMC Program.
Computer-based control of machine tools and manufacturing equipment through programmed numerical instructions.
The professional conduct requirements governing ethical and professional behavior for applicable participants in the CMMC assessment and certification ecosystem.
An organization that delivers cloud-based computing capabilities or services to customers.
Unclassified information that requires safeguarding or dissemination controls under applicable law, regulation, or government-wide policy.
A Department of Defense agency responsible for contract administration and oversight of defense contractors throughout the acquisition lifecycle.

term: Represents any two-character CMMC Domain acronym
description: The two-character domain abbreviation appearing at the beginning of a CMMC security requirement identifier, such as AC for Access Control or IA for Identification and Authentication.
The Department of Defense supplement to the Federal Acquisition Regulation containing acquisition requirements specific to DoD contracts, including cybersecurity and CMMC requirements.
The network of organizations, facilities, people, and resources that provide products and services supporting Department of Defense missions.

term: Defense Industrial Base Cybersecurity Assessment Center
description: The DCMA organization that leads DoD contractor cybersecurity assessment efforts, including NIST SP 800-171 assessments and designated CMMC assessment responsibilities.
The United States federal department responsible for national defense and the department responsible for establishing and administering the CMMC Program.
A directive issued by the Department of Defense that provides guidance and policy for military operations and activities.
A Department of Defense cybersecurity governance and risk-management system used to support authorization, assessment, and management of cybersecurity information.
An external organization that provides services supporting an organization's information systems, cybersecurity, or CMMC environment.
The primary regulation containing uniform policies and procedures used by federal executive agencies to acquire supplies and services.
Information provided by or generated for the Federal Government under a contract that is not intended for public release.

term: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program
description: A federal program that provides a standardized approach for assessing and authorizing cloud computing products and services used by federal agencies.
Equipment furnished to a contractor by the government for use in performing a government contract.
The security domain concerned with identifying users and devices and verifying their identities before granting access to systems or information.
Systems used to monitor and control industrial processes, including supervisory control, distributed control, and programmable automation technologies.
Internet-connected sensing, computing, and control devices used in industrial and operational environments.
Networks of physical devices equipped with computing, sensing, communications, or actuation capabilities that exchange data or interact with their environments.
The security domain concerned with preparing for, detecting, analyzing, containing, recovering from, and reporting cybersecurity incidents.
A set of information resources organized for collecting, processing, maintaining, using, sharing, disseminating, or disposing of information.
An international standards organization that develops and publishes standards for electrical, electronic, and related technologies.

term: International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission
description: A designation used for standards jointly developed or published by ISO and IEC, including standards addressing information security, cybersecurity, and technology.
Equipment, systems, software, services, and related resources used for the acquisition, storage, processing, management, transmission, control, display, or exchange of data and information.
The portion of a CMMC security requirement identifier that specifies the CMMC level associated with the requirement.
The security domain concerned with controlling, monitoring, and protecting system maintenance activities, personnel, tools, and associated access.
The security domain concerned with protecting system media containing sensitive information throughout its use, storage, transport, sanitization, and disposal.

An external service provider that delivers ongoing cybersecurity services such as security monitoring, threat detection, incident support, vulnerability management, or security technology administration.
The federal agency that serves as Executive Agent for the Controlled Unclassified Information program and oversees government-wide CUI implementation.
The industry classification system used by federal statistical and acquisition processes to categorize establishments according to their primary business activities.

term: National Institute of Standards and Technology
description: A U.S. Department of Commerce agency that develops standards, guidelines, measurements, and technology used across government and industry, including cybersecurity guidance supporting CMMC.
An assessment finding indicating that a security requirement or assessment objective does not apply to the organization or assessment scope at the time of assessment.
A variable part of a security requirement or control that an organization must instantiate by assigning or selecting an organization-defined value.
source: NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 / NIST CSRC Glossary

description: An organization undergoing a CMMC assessment.
An organization seeking a CMMC certification assessment and certification.
Programmable systems and devices that interact with the physical environment or manage devices, processes, and events that produce changes in physical systems.
A transitional CMMC instructor trained, tested, and designated by the CAICO to teach eligible CCP and CCA candidates during the provisional-instructor period.
A Department of Defense enterprise environment providing electronic capabilities that support procurement, contract administration, invoicing, and related acquisition processes.
Information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either by itself or when combined with other information linked or linkable to that individual.
A programmable industrial control device used to automate and control machines, processes, and other operational equipment.
A document identifying cybersecurity deficiencies and the actions, resources, milestones, and schedule planned to correct them.
Federal law governing how federal agencies collect information from the public and intended to reduce unnecessary information-collection burden.
The CMMC domain concerned with identifying and evaluating risks to organizational operations, assets, and information so that appropriate responses can be established.
The federal government's primary system for entity registration and contractor information used in conducting business with the government.
The security domain concerned with protecting information transmitted by systems and safeguarding system boundaries, communications, and architectural components.
A computerized industrial control capability used to gather and process operational data and apply supervisory control, often across geographically dispersed systems.
source: NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 / NIST CSRC Glossary

description: The security domain concerned with identifying, reporting, and correcting system flaws, protecting against malicious code, and monitoring systems for security-relevant conditions.
Security technology that centralizes collection and analysis of logs and security-event information to support monitoring, detection, investigation, and response activities.
A NIST publication series used to issue technical guidance, recommendations, and cybersecurity requirements, including the SP 800-series.
Security-related information used to protect systems, assets, or information and support cybersecurity functions within the applicable CMMC context.
A Department of Defense system used to maintain and provide supplier performance and risk information, including cybersecurity assessment information used in DoD acquisition processes.
